## OwnCode v0.3.0

OwnCode now includes selectable browser and macOS desktop tools. Enable them in **Settings → Automation**. Both start disabled.

### Browser control

- Choose managed headless Chromium, visible Chrome or Brave, an attached CDP browser, or the bundled extension.
- Open isolated agent tabs or explicitly share existing tabs through the extension.
- Navigate pages, inspect elements, fill forms, select options, and upload files.
- Use hover, drag, right-click, double-click, scrolling, keyboard shortcuts, and browser dialogs.
- Capture screenshots for models that support image attachments.
- Keep owned tabs separate between agents and cancel queued actions.

Managed modes use an installed browser. They do not download a browser or require Node.js. Embedded mode means headless browser automation, not a browser pane inside the terminal.

### macOS desktop control

- List and activate applications, then inspect accessible elements.
- Click accessible elements or use pointer coordinates on the primary display.
- Drag, scroll, and send Command, Control, Option, and Shift shortcuts.
- Capture the primary display with coordinate scaling for resized images.
- Serialize desktop actions across workers and release mouse buttons after canceled input.

macOS requires Accessibility, Automation, and Screen Recording permissions where applicable. Windows and Linux desktop adapters are not included. Desktop delivery depends on application behavior and local permissions.

### Configuration and screenshots

Automation settings are global. Project configuration cannot enable device access. Existing permission checks apply to each action. Plan and read-only workers do not receive these tools.

Screenshot results reach vision-capable models. Shake compaction can archive screenshots from active context. Full captures remain in `~/.owncode/automation/screenshots`.

### Install or upgrade

```sh
brew update
brew install muratmirgun/tap/owncode
# For an existing installation:
brew upgrade owncode
```

To use existing Chrome or Brave tabs:

```sh
owncode browser setup
```

Load the bundled extension and pair it with OwnCode. See the [automation guide](https://github.com/muratmirgun/owncode/blob/v0.3.0/docs/automation.md) for setup and supported actions.

macOS and Linux archives support arm64 and x86_64. Debian and RPM packages are also available. Verify archives against `checksums.txt`.

### Validation

- Full Go race suite, `go vet`, and build passed.
- Managed Chrome and Brave extension tests passed against isolated local fixtures.
- Extension tests cover tab ownership and URL validation.
- Native event construction passed without posting desktop input.
- Installer tests passed. No model calls were used.

**Full changes:** https://github.com/muratmirgun/owncode/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0
